The **2012 Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council election** was held on **Thursday 3 May 2012** to elect members of **Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council** in Greater Manchester, England.

## Basic facts

- **Council:** Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council  
- **Election date:** 3 May 2012  
- **Seats contested:** 21 of 63 — one seat in each of Stockport’s 21 wards  
- **Voting system:** First-past-the-post  
- **Election cycle:** Stockport elects by thirds, with one councillor per ward elected in most years  
- **Result:** The Liberal Democrats remained the largest party but **lost their overall majority**, leaving the council under **no overall control**.

## Political context

Before 2012, Stockport had been one of the Liberal Democrats’ stronger local-government areas. The party had controlled the council, but the 2012 election came during a difficult national period for the Liberal Democrats, who were in coalition with the Conservatives at Westminster after the 2010 general election.

Labour made gains in Stockport, as they did in many parts of England in the 2012 local elections, while the Conservatives remained relatively stable in their stronger suburban areas. The **Heald Green Ratepayers**, a local residents’ group, also retained representation.

## Overall result

The election resulted in the Liberal Democrats losing enough seats to fall short of a majority on the 63-seat council.

### Council composition after the election

| Party/group | Seats after election |
|---|---:|
| Liberal Democrats | 31 |
| Labour | 21 |
| Conservatives | 8 |
| Heald Green Ratepayers | 3 |
| **Total** | **63** |

A majority on Stockport Council requires **32 seats**, so the Liberal Democrats, with 31, were one seat short.

## Seats won in the 2012 election

Of the 21 seats contested, the approximate distribution of seats won was:

| Party/group | Seats won in 2012 |
|---|---:|
| Liberal Democrats | 9 |
| Labour | 8 |
| Conservatives | 3 |
| Heald Green Ratepayers | 1 |

Labour’s performance was the key story of the election, as it gained several seats from the Liberal Democrats.

## Political control

- **Before the election:** Liberal Democrat control  
- **After the election:** No overall control  
- **Largest party:** Liberal Democrats  

Although the Liberal Democrats lost their majority, they remained the largest group on the council and continued to play the leading role in the administration.

## Significance

The 2012 election was significant because it ended the Liberal Democrats’ outright majority in Stockport. It reflected both local political shifts and the wider national decline in Liberal Democrat support after entering the coalition government with the Conservatives in 2010.

Labour’s gains showed a recovery in parts of the borough, especially in more urban and traditionally Labour-leaning areas such as Reddish, Brinnington, Edgeley and parts of central Stockport.

The Conservatives remained strongest in more affluent suburban areas such as Bramhall, Cheadle Hulme South and related wards, while the Heald Green Ratepayers continued their distinctive local presence in Heald Green.

## Stockport’s ward structure at the time

Stockport had 21 wards, each represented by three councillors. The wards were:

- Bramhall North  
- Bramhall South and Woodford  
- Bredbury and Woodley  
- Bredbury Green and Romiley  
- Brinnington and Central  
- Cheadle and Gatley  
- Cheadle Hulme North  
- Cheadle Hulme South  
- Davenport and Cale Green  
- Edgeley and Cheadle Heath  
- Hazel Grove  
- Heald Green  
- Heatons North  
- Heatons South  
- Manor  
- Marple North  
- Marple South  
- Offerton  
- Reddish North  
- Reddish South  
- Stepping Hill  

One seat was up for election in each ward.

## Main takeaway

The **2012 Stockport Council election** marked a turning point in the borough’s politics. The Liberal Democrats remained the largest party but lost their council majority, Labour advanced, and Stockport moved into **no overall control**.
